regions.title: Ceres field
regions.blurb: The largest object in the asteroid belt, moving against the background stars.

regions.title: Eunomia field
regions.blurb: The largest stony asteroid, caught moving between frames.

regions.title: Hygiea field
regions.blurb: The fourth largest asteroid, drifting across the field.

regions.title: Iris field
regions.blurb: A bright main-belt asteroid caught in several SPHEREx frames.

regions.title: Juno field
regions.blurb: A bright main-belt asteroid caught in several SPHEREx frames.

regions.title: Pallas field
regions.blurb: Real SPHEREx frames from 6–14 Oct 2025. The asteroid (2) Pallas drifts across the field: blink it, then try to find it blind.

regions.title: Pallas patch, six months apart
regions.blurb: The same patch of sky in two survey passes six months apart. Stars stay put; a distant body would shift by parallax.

regions.title: Psyche field
regions.blurb: A metal-rich asteroid and NASA mission target, caught moving between frames.

regions.title: Practice field
regions.blurb: Simulated data with a planted mover and two survey passes 90 days apart. Not SPHEREx data: use it to learn the technique.

regions.title: Vesta field
regions.blurb: The second most massive asteroid, caught drifting between SPHEREx visits.
